assumptions: prefix_sha256 basis is the canonical JSON of the messages list (sort_keys, compact separators, utf-8), named on every row via prefix_sha256_basis; it is the exact list json.dumps'd into the POST body the server tokenises.
cached is None only when prompt_tokens_details (or its cached_tokens) is absent; a present cached_tokens=0 stays an observed miss (cached=0, usage_has_details=true).
uncached is None whenever cached is None; the analyser reports total_cached, total_uncached and mean_uncached as None unless every row of the chain was observed, and always reports n_unobserved.
Pass 1 salt is battery_salt(seed*1000+turn) (first sight per turn); pass 2 salt is battery_salt(seed) over the same rendered bytes, so pass 2 is the repeat of pass 1 (asserted in test_R5).

Compaction geometry fixed offline: COMPACT_KEEP_LAST=4, trigger at 3000 estimated tokens (default_est_tokens about 4 chars/token), so the first fold lands at turn 6 for every arm; the summariser is a deterministic stub (no model, no network).

Arm identity is asserted on POSTed bytes (at least 2 distinct prefix_sha256 per turn; measured 4 of 4) and on the declared plus observed plan carried in prompt_nodes: A/H share a policy so they may share a plan, every other pair must differ.

ARM_RENDER maps APPEND_NOTE to POINTER, SUMMARISE_IN_PLACE to NAIVE_APPEND and FORK to POINTER_FORK. POINTER and NAIVE_APPEND are equal-information on one chain, so A-vs-C body divergence comes from the in-place rewrite; documented, not engineered away.
phase_grid returns 'usage-unobserved' when the identical-prompt gate carries no usage details, and run_config then skips baseline/battery rather than recording blind zeros.

analysis_guard compares provenance: the existing file's _source.submitted_rows_sha256 (or, for a legacy file with no digest, its per-chain row counts) against the rows on disk BEFORE the write; FORCE is set only by run_analyse --force, never at import.
The live battery was not run and no container was touched, per the card; every claim above is offline evidence.
